Recode a categorical column by explicit name-to-name mapping

Source: R/categorical_guard.R
grdrcd.Rd

Recodes a categorical variable with a mapping written out by name, old_label = "new_label", so that the recode cannot depend on the order of the levels. Any value that the mapping does not cover is an error unless you list it in keep; nothing is silently set to NA or passed through. The result records the mapping and its SHA-256, so the recode that was applied can be shown later. Use it for collapsing or renaming categories (race, offence type, region) before analysis.

Usage

grdrcd(x, map, keep = character())

Arguments

x

A factor or character vector. Other atomic vectors are compared by matching the values that as.character() gives.

map

Named character vector, c(old_label = "new_label", ...). Every name must be non-empty.

keep

Character vector, default empty. Labels allowed to pass through unchanged.

Value

A character vector the same length as x, with a recode_audit attribute: a list with mapping (the mapping as given), kept (the keep vector) and checksum (hexadecimal SHA-256 of the mapping).

Details

Let \(S\) be the set of distinct non-missing values of x. The function refuses unless \(S \subseteq\) names(mapping) \(\cup\) keep. Each value found in names(mapping) is replaced by its mapped label; values in keep are returned unchanged; NA stays NA. Several old labels may map to the same new label (a collapse). Matching is exact: case and whitespace count.

The checksum is csha256 of the string "old1=new1;old2=new2;..." built from the mapping in its given order, so the same mapping written in a different order has a different checksum.

Errors: map not a character vector with non-empty names; any observed value that is neither mapped nor kept (the message lists them).

relbl is the same check but returns a factor; vrfrcd proves the result against the declared mapping; rcdmnf records it.

See also

vrfrcd to prove the recode, grdlvls to fix the levels, rcdmnf to record the chain.

Examples

# rename three codes
x <- c("W", "B", "O", "W", NA)
grdrcd(x, c(W = "White", B = "Black", O = "Other"))
#> [1] "White" "Black" "Other" "White" NA     
#> attr(,"recode_audit")
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$mapping
#>       W       B       O 
#> "White" "Black" "Other" 
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$kept
#> character(0)
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$checksum
#> [1] "992b6c4a35a3cea9e5875c90f562a3259fe9f08f1eb2fac9754d7c5b5f52bdd3"
#> 

# collapse two categories and let one pass through unchanged
off <- c("assault", "robbery", "theft", "fraud")
grdrcd(off, c(assault = "violent", robbery = "violent",
                    theft = "property"), keep = "fraud")
#> [1] "violent"  "violent"  "property" "fraud"   
#> attr(,"recode_audit")
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$mapping
#>    assault    robbery      theft 
#>  "violent"  "violent" "property" 
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$kept
#> [1] "fraud"
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$checksum
#> [1] "99dadc6bdace7a9f59469d16f31b7450e4f83835c9383bcbe1074ba84007706d"
#> 

# a value with no mapping is an error
try(grdrcd(x, c(W = "White", B = "Black")))
#> Error : grdrcd: values with NO mapping: ‘O’. Every observed category must be mapped by name (or listed in `keep`); silent pass-through is how group labels get corrupted.
